uncited: *   **Input:** A tetrahedron $T$ defined by four vertices; a discrete scalar field $F$ sampled at specific locations; the set of sample points $x$ that lie within $T$.
The method operates on the geometric definition of the tetrahedron and the scalar values at its vertices and internal sample points.
No complex data structures are required beyond standard vector/matrix representations for vertex positions and scalar arrays for field values.
Identify the set of original sample points $\{x_i\}$ from the scalar field $F$ that lie within the volume of tetrahedron $T$.
For each sample point $x_i$, determine its barycentric coordinates relative to the vertices of $T$.
Compute the interpolated value $f(x_i)$ by linearly interpolating the scalar values at the four vertices of $T$ using the barycentric coordinates.
Calculate the squared difference between the original field value $F(x_i)$ and the interpolated value $f(x_i)$.
Sum these squared differences over all sample points $x_i$ within $T$.
Normalize the sum by the volume of the tetrahedron $|T|$ to obtain the mean square error.
*   $|T|$ is the volume spanned by tetrahedron $T$.
*   $F(x)$ is the original scalar field value at sample point $x$.
*   $f(x)$ is the value at $x$ linearly interpolated from the values at the vertices of $T$.
*   The summation is over all sample values of $F$ at vertices $x$ that lie in $T$.
This is because EMS measures geometric approximation error of the field, not the relevance of the field to a specific isovalue.
*   **Screen-Space Projection:** The raw EMS is a volume-based metric.
*   **Scaling:** The metric is local to each tetrahedron, making it suitable for parallel evaluation during adaptive refinement.
